question: Show monthly revenue and order count for an accessible brand.
sql:
SELECT
  DATE_TRUNC(DATE(oi.created_at), MONTH) AS month,
  SUM(CAST(oi.sale_price AS NUMERIC)) AS revenue,
  COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id) AS order_count
FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.order_items` AS oi
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.orders` AS o
  ON o.order_id = oi.order_id AND o.user_id = oi.user_id
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.products` AS p
  ON p.id = oi.product_id
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.users` AS u
  ON u.id = oi.user_id
WHERE o.status = 'Complete'
  AND oi.status = 'Complete'
  AND p.brand = @brand
  AND DATE(oi.created_at) >= @start_date
  AND DATE(oi.created_at) < @end_date
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month
method: Use completed order items, count distinct orders, group by item creation month, and disclose the date and brand scope.
report: Compare only visible months. Cite visible strongest and weakest months, state that suppressed groups cannot be inferred, and avoid causal claims.

question: Compare two products during the same quarter.
sql:
SELECT
  p.name AS product,
  SUM(CAST(oi.sale_price AS NUMERIC)) AS revenue,
  COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id) AS order_count,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(
    SUM(CAST(oi.sale_price AS NUMERIC)),
    COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id)
  ) AS aov
FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.order_items` AS oi
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.orders` AS o
  ON o.order_id = oi.order_id AND o.user_id = oi.user_id
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.products` AS p
  ON p.id = oi.product_id
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.users` AS u
  ON u.id = oi.user_id
WHERE o.status = 'Complete'
  AND oi.status = 'Complete'
  AND p.brand = @brand
  AND LOWER(p.name) IN UNNEST(@products)
  AND DATE(oi.created_at) >= @start_date
  AND DATE(oi.created_at) < @end_date
GROUP BY product
ORDER BY revenue DESC
method: Use the same date window and metrics for both products, group by product, and compare revenue, order count, and AOV.
report: Describe observed differences, label possible explanations as hypotheses, and propose a next step using supported metrics and dimensions.

question: Compare this quarter with the previous quarter.
sql:
WITH scoped_items AS (
  SELECT
    oi.order_id,
    CAST(oi.sale_price AS NUMERIC) AS sale_price,
    DATE(oi.created_at) AS event_date
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.order_items` AS oi
  JOIN `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.orders` AS o
    ON o.order_id = oi.order_id AND o.user_id = oi.user_id
  JOIN `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.products` AS p
    ON p.id = oi.product_id
  JOIN `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.users` AS u
    ON u.id = oi.user_id
  WHERE o.status = 'Complete'
    AND oi.status = 'Complete'
    AND p.brand = @brand
    AND DATE(oi.created_at) >= @previous_start_date
    AND DATE(oi.created_at) < @current_end_date
), labeled AS (
  SELECT
    order_id,
    sale_price,
    CASE
      WHEN event_date < @current_start_date THEN 'previous'
      ELSE 'current'
    END AS comparison_period
  FROM scoped_items
)
SELECT
  comparison_period,
  SUM(sale_price) AS revenue,
  COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS order_count,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(SUM(sale_price), COUNT(DISTINCT order_id)) AS aov
FROM labeled
GROUP BY comparison_period
ORDER BY comparison_period
method: Use two non-overlapping half-open periods with identical filters and metric definitions.
report: State absolute values and percentage change only when the denominator is non-zero. Mention incomplete periods.
